classification.difficultyReason: Label the supplied tree from bag counts, perform explicitly requested path products, and group same-colour or different-colour outcomes for prompted addition.

content.prompt: One bag contains three red and two blue balls and another bag contains two red and three blue balls. A ball is drawn at random from each bag.

inlines.text: Complete the tree diagram by writing the probabilities on the branches.

spec.description: Binary tree with Start, Bag 1 and Bag 2; R precedes B at every split. Teacher probabilities are omitted from the question figure.
spec.mathematics: Two independent selections, one from each bag; six branches and four terminal paths RR, RB, BR and BB.
spec.answerVisibility: Branch probabilities are responses and appear only in answers.

answer.short: Bag 1: $P(R)=\frac35$, $P(B)=\frac25$. Bag 2 after either first outcome: $P(R)=\frac25$, $P(B)=\frac35$.
answer.worked: Each bag contains five balls. Bag 1 has three red and two blue balls, so its branches are $\frac35$ and $\frac25$. Bag 2 has two red and three blue balls, so its branches are $\frac25$ and $\frac35$ after either Bag 1 outcome. Selecting from Bag 1 does not change Bag 2.

spec.description: Complete probability tree with all six branch probabilities, reconstructed in ordinary black.
spec.mathematics: First split 3/5 and 2/5; both second-stage splits 2/5 and 3/5.
